key_insight: Experts perceived the AI as a mathematics-learning peer primarily through its social behavior, including non-judgmental interaction, tentative reasoning, and shared control.
engineering_relevance: Peer-oriented learning agents should prioritize collaborative dialogue, learner pacing, and calibrated disagreement rather than defaulting to tutor-like instruction.
method: Built an adaptive LLM peer combining a Big Five-informed persona with motivational state modulation.
Examined expert interactions and perceptions during collaborative mathematics problem solving.
Used thematic analysis of expert interviews to identify conditions supporting peer perceptions.
evidence_signal: Expert interview themes linked peer perceptions to emotional safety and appropriate imperfection, while blind agreement and over-instruction undermined trust.
watch_item: The abstract reports expert perceptions, not measured student learning gains, so classroom effectiveness remains unestablished.
paper_title: Exploring AI Peer in Collaborative Mathematics Learning
